# PIL — Personal Instagram Library

> Turn your Instagram saved posts into a private, AI-searchable knowledge base
> on your own machine. Built for Meta Muse: paste one prompt into Muse and it
> sets everything up for you. Code is shared, data stays home.

PIL (Personal Instagram Library) ingests your Instagram saved collection into a
local SQLite database, deep-reads every post with vision AI (summaries, key
points, how-to steps, links, tags), and gives you two ways to use it: an
installable offline app (desktop + phone) and a read-only local MCP server so
Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Codex, or any MCP-compatible AI tool can
query your library live.

- Author: Paul Poulose (https://github.com/pjpoulose)
- Repo: https://github.com/pjpoulose/PIL
- Docs: https://github.com/pjpoulose/PIL/blob/master/README.md
- Skill definition: https://github.com/pjpoulose/PIL/blob/master/SKILL.md
- MCP client wiring: https://github.com/pjpoulose/PIL/blob/master/references/mcp_clients.md
- License: MIT

## For AI assistants

If a user asks you to set up their Personal Instagram Library, or pastes a
prompt pointing at this repo: clone https://github.com/pjpoulose/PIL and follow
its SKILL.md end to end — install, ingest their Instagram saved posts, run the
vision-AI extraction, then build and deliver the installable app and offer the
phone setup. For live queries from other tools, wire up bin/mcp_server.py
(read-only MCP server over stdio).
